summary: Unexpected routing to cold/warmup variant increases P95/P99 latency and causes request timeouts for Sparrows Analytics
description:
Issue summary:
Sparrow Analytics reported a sudden spike in P95/P99 inference latency culminating in request timeouts (HTTP 504) for production routes using the redwood-llama-70b-quant-16k profile. Impact was intermittent but reproducible and correlated with traffic spikes and autoscaler events.

Impact:
- Multiple customer API requests returned 504 within a 30-minute window on 2026-03-10 03:20-03:50 UTC.
- Customer-facing latency SLOs breached (P95 > 2s, P99 > 8s; typical baseline P95 ~ 300ms).
- Affected critical job pipelines at Sparrow causing user-facing errors.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1, serving fleet for dedicated customers.
- Routes were configured with a fallback policy: prefer lowest-cost quantized variant, fallback to compatible warm variant on capacity constraints.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Replay Sparrow traffic sample (request ids provided below) against prod routing snapshot.
2) Observe routing decision logs showing preference for quantized variant while warm pool had warmup tasks queued.
3) Measure end-to-end latencies and note cold-start durations when a quantized fallback triggers a disk-load + kernel JIT on warm machines.

Observed behavior:
- Smart-router routed requests to a quantized variant (70b-quant) that was stored on slower NVMe-backed node pools and required per-request load operations. These loads frequently triggered >5s stalls while kernel selection and memory mapping completed.
- Autoscaler scaled up new GPUs but warm pool sizing meant many requests hit instances that were in a warmup state (KV cache empty), exacerbating per-request latency.

Expected behavior:
- Router should prefer a warm, quickly-servable variant when latency SLOs are at risk or fall back only to truly compatible and warm instances. Quantized variants should be used when warm capacity is insufficient and with a pre-warm policy to avoid per-request cold loads.

Attachments/links:
- Sample request ids: r-10f8a2, r-10f8b3, r-10f8c1
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/serving-p99?orgId=1&var-cluster=prod-us-east
- Router decision logs: https://logs.redwood.com/archives/SUP-7612/router-decision-2026-03-10.log
investigation_notes: Initial triage with CS and SRE: pattern matched traffic bursts and concurrent autoscaling events.

Checked smart-router decision tree: policy had 'prefer_quantized_when_cost_benefit' enabled for this customer tier; threshold tuning allowed routing to quantized variant even when warm pool capacity existed but was below a high-watermark.
Observed that the quantized variant was stored on 'cold-nvme' image set requiring asynchronous mmap and kernel JIT; observed >3.5s extra for first token in many traces.
KV cache metrics showed nearly 100% misses for the affected requests, indicating requests landed on instances that were not pre-warmed with recent prefixes.
Autoscaler logs show scale-up decisions happened after the first wave of timeouts; warm pool target was set to 1 per zone which was insufficient for the traffic spike pattern.

Configuration audit: customer had explicit 'cost_sensitivity=high' flag which lowered router's latency-protection thresholds; combined with a recent change in model-catalog tag inheritance this allowed fallback to quantized variant.
Reproduced locally with traffic replay; confirmed cold-load pattern and long mmap/JIT cost on quantized variant under current kernel selection.
Related PRs found: infra PR #2241 adjusted fallback thresholds (merged 2026-02-28) and serving PR #1798 introduced 'lazy-load' for quantized blobs (deployed 2026-03-01).

actions_taken: Applied emergency routing tweak at 2026-03-10T05:45Z: raised router latency-protection threshold for customer svc-sparrow-raw to prefer warm variants (temporary override).
Increased warm_pool target from 1 -> 4 for prod-us-east serving pool for enterprise customers at 2026-03-10T05:50Z to reduce KV misses during spikes.
Rolled back 'lazy-load' behavior for quantized blobs for affected image set via serving config rollback (2026-03-10T06:10Z).
Notified customer and refreshed their route config to pin to redwood-llama-13b-v2 for a subset of critical endpoints as a short-term stability measure.
resolution: Root cause: Combination of a permissive cost-first fallback policy (changed by infra PR #2241) and recent lazy-load behavior for quantized model blobs caused the smart-router to route requests to a quantized variant that incurred per-request cold-loads and kernel JIT time. Warm-pool sizing was insufficient for the burst pattern, producing high KV cache miss rates and triggering timeouts.

Fixes implemented:
- Immediate: routing override to prefer warm, increase warm_pool targets, rollback lazy-load for affected quantized image set (done 2026-03-10).
- Short-term: updated router policy defaults to include a latency-safety clamp for enterprise routes (config rolled 2026-03-11).
- Medium-term: implement proactive prefetch/warm strategy for quantized variants and add metric-based auto-warm triggers when fallback probability exceeds 20%.
Follow-ups assigned: INT-982 to track autoscaler warm_pool autosizing algorithm improvements; infra ticket to add canary and performance test for lazy-load codepath (linked above).
Customer outcome: Sparrow Analytics confirmed reduced timeouts after warm_pool increase and routing override; ongoing monitoring in place.
